hooks.text: A distant dying star exploded brightly enough to see.
Could you spot a stellar explosion halfway across the universe?
A single dying star briefly outshone ten million galaxies combined.

title: The Star You Could See 7.5 Billion Light-Years Away
description: Discover how a dying star 7.5 billion light-years away exploded with such fury it became visible from Earth to the naked eye.

beats.text: A distant dying star exploded brightly enough to see.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image showing the fading optical counterpart of GRB 080319B, 2008

beats.text: The flash came from 7.5 billion light-years away in the cosmos.
beats.visual: European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope facility, Chile, 2008

beats.text: It beamed right from the constellation Boötes.
beats.visual: Constellation Boötes night sky map by IAU

beats.text: For nearly a minute, it outshone ten million galaxies combined.
beats.visual: Illustration of a massive star collapsing into a black hole during a hypernova, NASA
queries: Massive star black hole jet illustration

beats.text: This brightness came from a jet shooting at 99.99995 percent light speed.
beats.visual: Illustration of a gamma-ray burst jet pointed toward Earth, NASA

beats.text: The cosmic blowtorch pointed directly down the barrel at Earth.
beats.visual: Diagram of a two-component gamma-ray burst jet structure, NASA
queries: GRB jet narrow and wide cone

beats.text: That is why you could see a distant dying star explode.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image showing the fading optical counterpart of GRB 080319B, 2008
